story.en:
Shani Travels is the ground-transport arm of the Shani Group of Companies, serving Pakistan since 1997. What began as a small chauffeur-driven car hire service in Islamabad has grown into a nationwide operation trusted by UN agencies, donors, NGOs, telecoms, airlines and government institutions.

We run project fleets through every province — from election observation missions and earthquake relief to multi-year development programmes and airline crew operations — backed by offices in 8 cities, vetted drivers and a maintenance regime that keeps every vehicle inspection-ready.

ceoMessage.en: For nearly three decades our promise has stayed the same: a clean, insured vehicle, a professional driver and a team that answers the phone. Whether you need one car for an airport pickup or forty vehicles for a nationwide programme, we treat both with the same seriousness.

hseSummary.en:
## Health, Safety & Environment

- Every vehicle GPS-tracked and comprehensively insured
- Documented pre-trip inspection for each journey
- Background-checked, defensively-trained drivers with route inductions
- Journey management and provincial backup vehicles for project fleets
- Incident reporting with 24/7 operations support

text.en: The 2026 rate card is live — transparent per-day rates on every vehicle.

commercialTerms.en:
## Commercial terms

- All rates are in PKR and **exclude General Sales Tax (GST)**.
- Daily rates cover a standard 10-hour working day within city limits; overtime is billed per additional hour.
- Fuel is billed per kilometre where marked; long routes include driver daily allowance.
- Intercity and northern-area trips may carry toll, parking and overnight charges at actuals.
- Bookings are confirmed by our team over phone or WhatsApp — no advance online payment is required.
- Corporate accounts are invoiced monthly with agreed credit terms.
- Rates marked "on request" are quoted per requirement after a short call.
- Self-drive rentals carry a security deposit and are subject to the self-drive agreement.
